title: Lanternwood Folk Fest program package: neutralize eight mixed-light performer photos to an in-frame grey card and a shared warm-amber house grade, triage a mixed bag of sponsor marks into vectorize-vs-lift, prep-and-trace the festival wordmark, then data-merge an authored InDesign template into one press-ready artist page per set and one recognition card per sponsor
grounding_note: Adapted from a real Freelancer.com brief ("Event Program Booklet / Brochure Design": a client 'producing a booklet-style brochure that will double as the official program guide', wanting 'careful proofreading, alignment and image optimisation for print', a 'press-ready PDF', and 'every logo crisp, proportionate and consistently placed, with plenty of white space so partners look their best') and laundered to a fictional two-day roots-and-Americana festival, 'Lanternwood Folk Fest' — no real company, person, org, or trademark is named. REPOSITIONED for connector reality: the original brief implies a from-scratch multi-page layout AND a multi-sponsor grid on one page, NEITHER of which is connector-doable — document_merge_data_layout emits exactly ONE FILE PER ROW (it cannot place several records on a shared page, so a multi-sponsor grid is impossible) and a convert_pdf_to_indd template will not bind merge fields. So the client is modeled as supplying two genuinely hand-authored SINGLE-RECORD InDesign templates (an interior artist-feature page and a sponsor recognition card), each carrying live <<fields>> plus @-prefixed image-path columns, two rosters, a folder of raw performer press photos shot across two evenings under mismatched light (each with a photographic 18% grey card laid in frame), a mixed folder of raw sponsor logo source files, and a flat scan of the festival wordmark. The Adobe chain does the real work the brief rewards: neutralize every performer photo to its own in-frame grey card and drive the whole set to one shared white point under a deliberate warm-amber 'lantern' house grade the agent authors and propagates, decide per sponsor mark whether to vectorize it (flat rasters) or lift it onto a clean transparent PNG (marks photographed on a busy ground), prep-and-trace the scanned wordmark, then run each authored template through a one-file-per-row data-merge — one artist page per performance set and one recognition card per sponsor — and export press-ready and screen PDFs. No deliverable is invented beyond the program package the brief asks for; all copy binds verbatim from the rosters.
one_line_ask: Grade eight mixed-lighting performer press photos to the 18% grey card each one carries and to a shared warm-amber festival house look (deciding per frame how far to move white balance without wrecking any act's true color), prep the festival's sponsor marks — the right way for each — get the scanned festival wordmark crisp and razor-sharp, then data-merge the client's two authored single-record InDesign templates against the schedule and the sponsor list to produce one press-ready artist page per set and one recognition card per sponsor, plus a screen PDF of the interior for the event app.
full_brief: Lanternwood Folk Fest, a fictional two-day roots-and-Americana music festival, needs its official program package finished for print and for the event app. We are handing you the pieces; we are NOT reshooting or re-designing. Here is the work. FIRST, the performer photos: eight press shots, one per act on the bill, came in from a handful of different photographers over two evenings — some under cool stage-wash, some under warm tungsten in the green room, one in flat open shade, one washed-out and overexposed, a couple with a greenish house-light cast, a couple tilted. Straight out of the folder they read as a mismatched jumble, and a program of mismatched shots looks cheap. To make this checkable we laid a photographic 18% grey card into the corner of every shot. Bring every image to a consistent, true-to-act look by neutralizing each one to the grey card it contains — the card must read as a clean neutral grey (equal across the channels) in your finished frame, and once every card is neutral the whole set shares one white point. THEN, on top of that neutral base, give the set our festival's signature look: a warm, lantern-lit amber feel — a gentle warmth in the highlights, restrained vibrance, tone that glows without going orange — established once and carried consistently across all eight so they feel like one shoot. Do NOT force one blanket slider move across the batch: each photo was lit differently and needs its own white-balance, exposure and tone decision to land on the shared neutral base before the house look goes on. Be careful — at least one act was genuinely shot at golden hour and is SUPPOSED to look warm; if its grey card already reads neutral, do not 'cool' it chasing an imagined cast, or you will strip the very warmth that makes the shot. When you're done, tell us the final white-balance and exposure move you made on each frame so we can confirm they're matched, not eyeballed. SECOND, the sponsor marks: our partners sent their logos in whatever form they had — some are clean flat art files, some are just a phone photo of the logo on a storefront window or a printed banner. Every logo must end up crisp, proportionate and print-safe and sit consistently on the cream page with plenty of white space, so partners look their best. Get each one clean the way that mark actually needs — a flat art file and a photographed-on-a-busy-background logo are NOT the same job, and choosing wrong is invisible until it's on the printer. THIRD, our festival wordmark only exists as a flat scan on kraft paper — get it clean and razor-sharp for the page mastheads and the sponsor cards; it must not print like a fuzzy scan. FOURTH, source a subtle kraft/recycled-paper texture to back the pages, in keeping with our look. FINALLY, build the pieces: we have hand-built two InDesign templates with the real placeholder fields and image slots — an interior ARTIST FEATURE page (one act per page: day, stage, set time, act name, one-line bio, the act's photo, the festival wordmark in the masthead, the kraft ground behind) and a sponsor RECOGNITION card (one sponsor per card: sponsor name, tier, the prepped logo, the wordmark, the kraft ground) — and we're giving you the schedule roster and the sponsor list. Merge them so every set gets its own artist page with its copy bound and its matching graded photo dropped in, and every sponsor gets its own recognition card with its prepped logo dropped in, then hand back a press-ready ~300 DPI CMYK PDF of the artist pages (one page per set, with bleed/crop marks), a matching press-ready CMYK PDF of the sponsor cards (one card per sponsor), and a lighter RGB screen-quality PDF of the artist pages for the event app. Bind all copy verbatim from the rosters — do not rewrite our bios, names or tiers. Acceptance: every grey card neutral and the whole photo set matched to one white point under the shared warm-amber house look; every sponsor mark print-safe by the correct method; the wordmark a crisp vector; and exactly one finished page per roster row.

inputs.name: lanternwood_interior_template.indd
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED DELIVERABLE (cannot be model-generated): a genuine, hand-built Adobe InDesign document (.indd/.idml) for a SINGLE-RECORD A5 (148x210mm) portrait ARTIST FEATURE page — ONE performance set per page — in the festival's established warm-cream / lantern-amber identity and type hierarchy. It must contain live InDesign data-merge placeholder fields <<day>>, <<stage>>, <<set_time>>, <<artist>>, <<bio>>, and THREE @-prefixed image-path merge columns wired to three separate image frames: an artist-photo frame bound to @artist_photo (that set's graded press photo, sized to a 4:5 portrait ratio), a masthead frame bound to @festival_mark (the vectorized festival wordmark), and a full-bleed background frame bound to @paper_ground (the licensed kraft texture). Because free-form image-at-coordinates placement is banned, the wordmark and the kraft ground reach the page ONLY as merge binds through their image columns — they are not dropped in by hand. Built by hand in InDesign so the merge fields and all three image frames actually bind. Explicitly NOT a convert_pdf_to_indd output and NOT a multi-record grid: document_merge_data_layout emits one file per row, so the template holds exactly one record's worth of fields.
inputs.realism_notes: document_merge_data_layout is [T] and REQUIRES a user-authored .indd carrying real merge fields plus genuine @image-path columns, and it emits ONE FILE PER ROW — so a per-set single-record artist page is the correct connector-doable shape (a 'booklet' of one act per page). Supplied as an input, not a chain output; a PDF-converted .indd with literal typed text would not bind. THREE image columns mean the merge resolves three prepped assets per row — the row's graded artist photo (@artist_photo, unique per row) plus the shared vectorized wordmark (@festival_mark) and shared kraft ground (@paper_ground, identical in every row) — so the chain-produced wordmark and licensed texture reach every page as merge binds without any free-form placement (mirrors AO-74's shared @Wordmark column).

inputs.name: lanternwood_sponsorcard_template.indd
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED DELIVERABLE (cannot be model-generated): a second genuine hand-built Adobe InDesign document (.indd/.idml) for a SINGLE-RECORD A5 portrait SPONSOR RECOGNITION card — ONE sponsor per card — in the same warm-cream / lantern-amber identity, with generous white space around the mark 'so partners look their best'. It must contain live merge fields <<sponsor_name>>, <<sponsor_tier>>, and THREE @-prefixed image-path columns: a logo frame bound to @sponsor_logo (that sponsor's prepped mark), a masthead frame bound to @festival_mark (the vectorized festival wordmark), and a full-bleed background frame bound to @paper_ground (the kraft texture). Built by hand so all fields and image frames bind. NOT a convert_pdf_to_indd output; NOT a multi-sponsor grid — a grid of several sponsors on one page is impossible under a one-file-per-row merge, so each sponsor gets its own card.
inputs.realism_notes: Separate authored single-record template because the sponsor grid the original brief implied (many logos on one back-cover page) is NOT connector-doable — the merge places one record per page. The @sponsor_logo column binds the AGENT's prepped mark named per the agent's own triage (see the sponsor sources); @festival_mark and @paper_ground are the same shared assets as the interior template. The sponsor's prepped file could be a vectorized SVG or a lifted transparent PNG depending on what the source needed — the template's logo frame accepts either — and nothing in this template or its roster reveals which sponsor got which treatment.

inputs.name: lanternwood_schedule.csv
inputs.gen_prompt: Generate a CSV with columns day,stage,set_time,artist,bio,@artist_photo,@festival_mark,@paper_ground holding 8 performance-set rows (one per act whose press photo is supplied): day is 'Saturday' or 'Sunday'; stage is 'Lantern Stage','Willow Stage' or 'Barn Stage'; set_time like '2:30 PM'; artist is a fictional folk/Americana act (e.g. 'The Copper Kettle Trio','Marigold & the Wandering Sons','Hollow Pines','The Ember Wren','Sawdust & Cedar','June Hollow','The Tanglewood Rounders','Ashgrove Bell'); bio is one appetizing sentence. The @artist_photo column names the AGENT's prepped graded crop for that set (e.g. @artist_graded_01.jpg ... @artist_graded_08.jpg) so the [T] merge drops each graded photo into that row's page. @festival_mark holds the SAME vectorized wordmark file (@lanternwood_wordmark.svg) in EVERY row; @paper_ground holds the SAME licensed kraft file in EVERY row. Column names must exactly match the interior template merge fields <<day>>,<<stage>>,<<set_time>>,<<artist>>,<<bio>> and the three @image-path columns @artist_photo,@festival_mark,@paper_ground.
inputs.realism_notes: Honors the brief's 'all copy... in your hands'; headers match the authored interior .indd fields and all three @-image columns so the one-file-per-row [T] merge binds copy, the correct graded photo, the shared wordmark, and the shared kraft ground per set. The @artist_photo entries name AGENT-produced graded outputs under a uniform scheme (all eight photos get the SAME grade treatment, so naming them in the roster encodes no triage answer). Eight rows => the merge must produce exactly eight artist pages.

inputs.name: lanternwood_sponsors.csv
inputs.gen_prompt: Generate a CSV with columns sponsor_name,sponsor_tier,@sponsor_logo,@festival_mark,@paper_ground holding 5 fictional sponsor rows (one per supplied logo source): sponsor_name like 'Harbormill Coffee Roasters','Cedarline Outfitters','Riverbend Mutual','Foxglove Cider Works','Northlight Instruments'; sponsor_tier is 'Presenting','Stage' or 'Community'. The @sponsor_logo column names the AGENT's prepped mark for that sponsor under a UNIFORM neutral basename scheme (@sponsor_prepped_01 ... @sponsor_prepped_05) — the basename carries NO extension and NO hint of whether the agent will fill it with a vectorized SVG or a lifted PNG. @festival_mark holds the same @lanternwood_wordmark.svg in every row; @paper_ground holds the same kraft file in every row. Column names must exactly match the sponsor-card template merge fields <<sponsor_name>>,<<sponsor_tier>> and the three @image-path columns.
inputs.realism_notes: Drives one recognition card per sponsor; headers match the authored sponsor-card .indd fields. CRITICAL no-telegraph: the @sponsor_logo entries are a UNIFORM neutral basename per sponsor (@sponsor_prepped_01..05) with no extension and no 'flat'/'photo' hint, so the supplied roster looks identical for all five sponsors and never reveals which mark must be vectorized vs lifted — the agent decides that per source, produces the prepped file, and uploads it under the referenced basename (the merge resolves basename->URN via additionalImageFiles regardless of whether the content is an SVG or a transparent PNG). Five rows => the merge must produce exactly five sponsor cards. Bound in a separate merge pass into the sponsor-card template.

inputs.name: capture_01.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL full-frame DSLR/mirrorless press photo, ~4000-4500 px on the long edge, of a three-piece folk/Americana band (banjo, upright bass, acoustic guitar) standing outside a weathered barn, with a photographic 18% grey card laid flat in one corner of the frame as a neutral reference. Cool bluish stage-wash cast, frame tilted ~4 degrees, real skin and clothing texture, candid documentary feel, no studio gloss, no CGI. The grey card is clearly visible and uncropped.
inputs.realism_notes: Cool cast + tilt => must be straightened AND warmed to neutralize its grey card to the shared white point. REAL-CAMERA scale (~4000-4500 px) so the 4:5 crop fills the page frame at ~300 DPI by DOWNSCALE ONLY — no upscaling. Neutral filename (capture_01) shares the scheme of all eight so the per-frame diagnosis lives only here, never in the filename.

inputs.name: capture_02.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL full-frame press photo, ~4000-4500 px long edge, of a folk duo seated on porch steps with a fiddle and a guitar, an 18% grey card laid in one corner. Warm tungsten green-room light (orange cast), level frame, underexposed dull shadows, candid, real texture, no gloss.
inputs.realism_notes: Warm tungsten cast => must move the OPPOSITE direction from the cool frames (COOL it) to neutralize its card, plus lift the dull shadows. Level, so no straighten. Proves the batch is not uniformly cool — a blanket 'warm everything' pass fails here.

inputs.name: capture_03.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL full-frame press photo, ~4000-4500 px long edge, of a solo singer-songwriter with an acoustic guitar in a field, 18% grey card in one corner. Near-neutral late-afternoon daylight, frame tilted ~3 degrees, clean exposure, candid, real detail.
inputs.realism_notes: Near-neutral light => its card is already close to neutral; only a SMALL white-balance nudge is needed to land on the shared point (over-correcting pushes it off the set). Tilted => straighten. A small-move frame among big-move frames.

inputs.name: capture_04.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL full-frame press photo, ~4000-4500 px long edge, of a solo singer standing in a field at genuine golden hour, warmly backlit, holding an acoustic guitar, with an 18% grey card laid flat in one corner shot under that same warm-but-neutral-balanced light so the card itself reads neutral. Level frame, rich warm skin and sky, candid, real detail, no CGI.
inputs.realism_notes: THE TRAP FRAME. The scene is genuinely warm (golden hour) but the shot was correctly balanced so its in-frame grey card ALREADY reads neutral. The correct move is essentially NO white-balance shift (only match exposure/brightness to the set, then the shared house look). A naive agent that batch-applies a 'warm the cool cast' correction, or 'cools an imagined cast', will push its card off-neutral and strip the real golden-hour warmth the shot is selling. Decision must be driven by THIS card, not the batch.

inputs.name: capture_05.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL full-frame press photo, ~4000-4500 px long edge, of a five-piece string band on a covered stage, 18% grey card in one corner. Flat open-shade light, noticeably underexposed and low-contrast, level frame, real texture, candid, no gloss.
inputs.realism_notes: Flat and underexposed => the dominant move is TONAL (lift exposure, add contrast/clarity) before a small WB neutralization to the shared point — a different problem axis from the cool/warm frames. Level, no straighten.

inputs.name: capture_06.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL full-frame press photo, ~4000-4500 px long edge, of a banjo-and-fiddle pair outdoors near sunset, 18% grey card in one corner. Overexposed and washed out with a blown bright sky, frame tilted ~3 degrees, real detail, candid.
inputs.realism_notes: Overexposed => PULL exposure/highlights down to recover the blown sky, then neutralize its card. Opposite tonal direction from the underexposed frame 05 — proving the batch needs per-frame reasoning. Tilted => straighten.

inputs.name: capture_07.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL full-frame press photo, ~4000-4500 px long edge, of a solo performer at a mic under a barn's house lights, 18% grey card in one corner. Greenish fluorescent house-light cast, level frame, otherwise reasonable exposure, real skin texture, candid.
inputs.realism_notes: Greenish cast => the corrective axis here is TINT (magenta, green/magenta) not temperature — a different axis again; neutralize the card by pulling green out, not by warming/cooling. Level, no straighten.

inputs.name: capture_08.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL full-frame press photo, ~4000-4500 px long edge, of a duo with a resonator guitar in open shade under a blue-hour sky, 18% grey card in one corner. Cool blue open-shade cast, level frame, clean exposure, real detail, candid.
inputs.realism_notes: Cool blue open-shade => warm it to neutralize its card to the shared point (a different magnitude of warm-move than frame 01's stage-wash cool). Level, no straighten. Eighth divergent frame in the matched set.

inputs.name: sponsor_source_01.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A flat two-color sponsor wordmark reading 'Harbormill Coffee Roasters' with a small coffee-bean-and-anchor emblem, solid dark-teal and cream on a transparent background, crisp flat high-contrast raster PNG, no gradients, clean edges.
inputs.realism_notes: Clean FLAT high-contrast art => the correct treatment is image_vectorize into a print-safe SVG that stays razor-sharp at any size. Neutral filename shares the sponsor_source_0N scheme; the vectorize-vs-lift diagnosis lives only in this note, never in the filename or extension.

inputs.name: sponsor_source_02.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A flat single-color sponsor logo reading 'Cedarline Outfitters' with a simple pine-tree mark, solid forest green on a transparent background, crisp flat high-contrast raster PNG, no gradients, clean vector-ready edges.
inputs.realism_notes: Flat single-color line art => vectorize to a clean scalable SVG. Same neutral scheme; treatment decided by opening it, not by its name.

inputs.name: sponsor_source_03.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A flat two-color sponsor lockup reading 'Foxglove Cider Works' with a simple apple-and-leaf mark, solid oxblood and warm gold on a transparent background, crisp flat high-contrast raster PNG, no gradients, clean edges.
inputs.realism_notes: Third FLAT art file => vectorize to SVG. Three flat rasters keep the vectorize sub-chain from being a single hero and let the triage be a real repeated decision, not a coin flip.

inputs.name: sponsor_source_04.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A photoreal phone snapshot of the 'Riverbend Mutual' logo (a blue river-wave mark and navy wordmark) printed on a glass storefront window, shot at a slight angle with reflections and a blurred street visible through the glass behind it. The logo itself is fully readable and unoccluded but sits on a busy real-world background. Natural daylight, candid documentary look. Saved as PNG.
inputs.realism_notes: Logo PHOTOGRAPHED on a busy ground => the correct treatment is LIFT (image_select_by_prompt the mark, then image_remove_background to a clean transparent PNG), NOT vectorize — feeding this photo to image_vectorize returns a garbage/blob trace of the reflections and street. Logo is fully visible/unoccluded so the lift is a clean cutout, no reconstruction/inpainting. Same .png extension as the flat art files so the triage cannot be read off the filename.

inputs.name: sponsor_source_05.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A photoreal photo of the 'Northlight Instruments' logo (a compass-star mark and slab wordmark) screen-printed on a rippled fabric event banner outdoors, shot slightly off-square with soft outdoor shadows and grass visible at the edges. The logo is fully readable and unoccluded but sits on a textured, uneven cloth background. Candid documentary look. Saved as PNG.
inputs.realism_notes: Second PHOTOGRAPHED-on-a-busy-ground mark => LIFT (select_by_prompt + remove_background) to a transparent PNG, not vectorize (the cloth ripple and grass would trace as noise). Two lift sources plus three vectorize sources mean the triage is a genuine 5-way decision the agent must make by opening each file; getting one wrong is invisible until the mark is on the printer.

inputs.name: lanternwood_wordmark_scan.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A flat desktop scan of the 'Lanternwood Folk Fest' wordmark inked on kraft/recycled paper: a warm hand-lettered serif with a small hanging-lantern mark, deep espresso-brown letters on the mottled kraft ground (NOT transparent, NOT pure white). Rendered as a real scan — the mark sits very slightly rotated (~2 deg) on the scan bed, there is extra kraft margin around it, and edges are a touch soft.
inputs.realism_notes: Scanned-on-kraft (kraft ground, slight rotation, margin, soft edges) so image_vectorize would trace the paper texture and the skew if fed raw — forcing genuine prep-before-trace: straighten, crisp/separate the lettering from the kraft, crop to the mark, knock the kraft ground to transparency, THEN vectorize. gemini-3-pro-image for clean legible lettering. Produces @lanternwood_wordmark.svg, bound into every artist page and sponsor card via @festival_mark.

outputs.name: Lanternwood_Program_Interior_press.pdf
outputs.spec: Press-ready ~300 DPI CMYK PDF of the eight interior artist-feature pages (page-count = schedule-row-count = 8), one performance set per page, exported from the one-file-per-row InDesign data-merge with bleed and crop marks; each page binds its day/stage/set_time/artist/bio verbatim from the schedule roster, with its matching grey-card-neutralized, house-graded 4:5 photo dropped into the artist frame (via @artist_photo), the vectorized festival wordmark in the masthead (via @festival_mark) and the licensed kraft ground behind (via @paper_ground) — all by merge bind, never free-form placement.

outputs.name: Lanternwood_Sponsor_Cards_press.pdf
outputs.spec: Press-ready ~300 DPI CMYK PDF of the five sponsor recognition cards (page-count = sponsor-row-count = 5), one sponsor per card, exported from a separate one-file-per-row merge; each card binds sponsor_name/sponsor_tier verbatim with that sponsor's prepped mark dropped in (via @sponsor_logo — a vectorized SVG or a lifted transparent PNG per the agent's triage), the wordmark (via @festival_mark) and the kraft ground (via @paper_ground). Generous white space so every mark sits crisp, proportionate and consistently placed.

outputs.name: graded_performer_photos
outputs.spec: Eight grey-card-neutralized, house-graded performer photos, delivered as the 4:5 artist-frame crops (grey card cropped OUT) that bind into the merge, alongside their RETAINED pre-crop neutralized masters (grey card still in frame) which the harness keeps as the neutrality-grading artifacts. Acceptance (grader-checked, two SEPARATE claims): (a) neutralisation is graded on the RETAINED pre-crop neutralized master of each frame (its in-frame 18% grey card still present) — the card region reads a clean neutral (per-channel spread within a hair of zero) with the whole set matched to one shared white point under the consistent warm-amber house look, and true-to-act (no act's genuine color forced off, the golden-hour frame's warmth held); (b) card-exclusion is checked separately on each delivered 4:5 crop (grey card fully cropped OUT). The neutrality tolerance is never evaluated on the card-removed crop. Accompanied by a report of the final white-balance and exposure move applied to each frame.

outputs.name: sponsor_logos_prepped
outputs.spec: Five print-safe sponsor marks, prepped by the correct method per source: the three flat-raster marks delivered as clean scalable SVGs (vectorized), and the two photographed-on-a-busy-ground marks lifted onto clean transparent-background PNGs (select_by_prompt + remove_background), so all five sit consistently on the cream recognition cards. Each is uploaded under its roster basename (@sponsor_prepped_01..05) for the merge.

outputs.name: lanternwood_wordmark.svg
outputs.spec: Clean vector SVG of the festival wordmark, traced only after the kraft scan is straightened, crisped, cropped to the mark, and knocked to transparency — razor-sharp at masthead scale with no captured kraft ground or skew. Bound into every artist page and sponsor card via @festival_mark.

connector_workflow.note: Search Adobe Stock for a subtle kraft/recycled-paper texture to back the pages, in keeping with the festival look (low-res candidates).
License and download the chosen kraft texture at full-res (license BEFORE use); becomes the shared @paper_ground bound behind every page.
Triage: this frame is tilted ~4 deg, so level it first. (Only the tilted frames 01/03/06 get straightened; the level frames skip this — deciding which is part of the job.)

Cool bluish stage-wash: WARM it (positive temperature) and set tint until the in-frame 18% grey card reads neutral (R=G=B), set exposure/highlights/shadows so the card sits mid-grey, THEN lay on the shared warm-amber house look (a gentle highlight warmth + restrained vibrance the agent authors on this reference frame and will carry across all eight) tuned so the neutral card patch stays neutral. Reason the exact temp/tint/exposure to THIS card — do not reuse another frame's numbers. Report the final move. Single primitive-built adjustments call (replaces deprecated image_adjust_color_temperature / _vibrance_and_saturation; NOT auto_tone).

Crop the neutralized frame to the 4:5 portrait the artist frame expects, framing on the act with the grey card cropped OUT — this crop binds into the page. The pre-crop neutralized master (cap01_neutralized, card still in frame) is RETAINED as the neutrality-grading artifact; neutrality is graded THERE, card-exclusion is the separate check here. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only, never generative-expand.

Warm tungsten green-room cast, level frame: move the OPPOSITE direction from the cool frames — COOL it (negative temperature) until its grey card reads neutral, lift the underexposed shadows, then apply the SAME shared warm-amber house look established on frame 01. Distinct numbers from frame 01 because the light differed. Report the move.
Crop to the 4:5 artist frame; grey card cropped OUT. Retain cap02_neutralized as the grading master. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.
Tilted ~3 deg — level it.

Near-neutral daylight: its card is already close to neutral, so only a SMALL WB nudge lands it on the shared white point — over-correcting pushes it off the set. Match exposure to set brightness, apply the house look. Report the (small) move.
Crop to the 4:5 artist frame; card cropped OUT. Retain cap03_neutralized. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.

THE TRAP FRAME. Genuine golden hour, but the shot was correctly balanced so its in-frame grey card ALREADY reads neutral. Correct move: essentially NO white-balance shift — only match exposure/brightness to the set and apply the shared house look. A naive agent that batch-applies the 'warm the cool cast' move from frame 01, or 'cools an imagined cast', neutralizes the card off-neutral and strips the real golden-hour warmth. Decision driven by THIS card, not the batch. Report that WB was held.
Crop to the 4:5 artist frame; card cropped OUT. Retain cap04_neutralized. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.

Flat open-shade and underexposed, level: the dominant move is TONAL — LIFT exposure, add contrast/clarity — then a small WB neutralization of its card to the shared point, then the house look. Different problem axis from the cool/warm frames. Report the move.
Crop to the 4:5 artist frame; card cropped OUT. Retain cap05_neutralized. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.
Tilted ~3 deg — level it.

Overexposed washed sky: PULL exposure/highlights down to recover the blown sky, then neutralize its card to the shared white point, then the house look. Opposite tonal direction from the underexposed frame 05. Report the move.
Crop to the 4:5 artist frame; card cropped OUT. Retain cap06_neutralized. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.

Greenish fluorescent house-light cast, level: the corrective axis here is TINT (pull green toward magenta) NOT temperature — neutralize the card by removing the green, hold exposure, apply the house look. A temperature-only correction leaves the card green and fails. Report the move.
Crop to the 4:5 artist frame; card cropped OUT. Retain cap07_neutralized. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.

Cool blue open-shade, level: WARM it to neutralize its card to the shared point (a different magnitude of warm-move than frame 01's stage-wash cool), then the house look. Eighth divergent frame — all eight now share one white point under one warm-amber look. Report the move.
Crop to the 4:5 artist frame; card cropped OUT. Retain cap08_neutralized. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.

TRIAGE decision: this source is clean FLAT high-contrast art, so the correct print-safe treatment is to VECTORIZE it into a scalable SVG (razor-sharp at any card size). Uploaded under basename sponsor_prepped_01 for the merge. A wrong route (lifting it as a low-res PNG) would print soft.
Flat single-color line art => vectorize to a clean SVG. Second vectorize decision (basename sponsor_prepped_02).
Third FLAT art file => vectorize to SVG (basename sponsor_prepped_03). Three separate vectorize decisions, not one hero.

TRIAGE decision: this source is a photo of the logo on busy storefront glass, so vectorizing it would trace the reflections/street into garbage — the correct treatment is to LIFT it. Semantically select just the 'Riverbend Mutual' river-wave mark and navy wordmark off the glass (fully visible/unoccluded). Not a hue/coordinate selection — a named object.

Lift the selected mark onto a clean transparent PNG so it sits consistently on the cream card (basename sponsor_prepped_04). remove_background -> transparency (NOT select->invert->fill); no reconstruction since the mark is unoccluded.

Second LIFT decision: this source is the logo on a rippled fabric banner (cloth texture + grass would trace as noise), so lift rather than vectorize. Select the 'Northlight Instruments' compass-star mark and slab wordmark off the banner.
Lift the selected mark onto a transparent PNG (basename sponsor_prepped_05). Two lifts + three vectorizes complete the 5-way sponsor triage; the roster reveals none of it.
Prep-before-trace step 1: the kraft scan sits ~2 deg rotated on the bed — straighten so the vector edges are square. Feeding the raw skewed scan to vectorize would bake in the rotation.
Prep-before-trace step 2: push contrast/clarity so the espresso lettering separates hard from the mottled kraft ground — a soft low-contrast scan traces into ragged, doubled edges.
Prep-before-trace step 3: crop away the kraft margin to the tight bounds of the mark so vectorize traces only the wordmark, not the paper field.
Prep-before-trace step 4: knock the kraft ground to transparency so the trace captures the letterforms and lantern mark only, not a rectangle of kraft. remove_background -> transparency.

Now trace the prepared raster (straightened, crisped, cropped, transparent) into a clean SVG for the mastheads and sponsor cards. Tracing the raw kraft scan instead would produce a skewed, paper-bounded, fuzzy silhouette — the trap this prep chain avoids.

chaining_note: Strict output-to-input chaining throughout. The kraft ground chains asset_search(1)->license(2). Eight per-photo grade sub-chains fan out from the raw captures, each an image_apply_adjustments neutralization-plus-house-look followed by a 4:5 crop, with image_auto_straighten inserted only on the tilted frames 01/03/06 — every neutralization is driven to that frame's own in-frame grey card so all eight converge on one shared white point, and the SAME agent-authored warm-amber look is laid on each (cool frames 01/08 warmed, warm frame 02 cooled, greenish frame 07 corrected on the tint axis, underexposed 05 lifted, overexposed 06 recovered, near-neutral 03 nudged small, golden-hour 04 held). The sponsor triage runs five decisions: the three flat rasters vectorize directly (sponsor_source_01->vectorize(22), _02->(23), _03->(24)) while the two photographed marks lift in two links each (sponsor_source_04->select_by_prompt(25)->remove_background(26); _05->select_by_prompt(27)->remove_background(28)). The wordmark runs a genuine prep-before-trace chain: straighten(29)->crisp adjustments(30)->crop_to_bounds(31)->remove_background to transparency(32)->vectorize(33). All eight graded photos, the five prepped sponsor marks, the wordmark SVG and the kraft ground converge into the upload session(34)->finalize(35). The finalized URNs plus the authored interior .indd and the schedule CSV feed the first merge(36) -> eight artist pages; the same URNs plus the authored sponsor-card .indd and the sponsor CSV feed the second merge(37) -> five sponsor cards. The interior merged set is exported twice — press(38) and screen(39) — and the sponsor set once(40). Two merge passes are used because document_merge_data_layout binds a single dataSourceUrl per call. Nothing after the stock search and the raw loads originates outside the chain.
difficulty_rationale: Long-horizon flagship with difficulty from DEPTH, not plumbing: 40 connector calls, 13 distinct Adobe tools across three groups (image_* grade/mask/vectorize, asset_* stock/storage, document_* merge/export), far above the >=10 call / >=6 distinct-tool floor even after stripping the 2 upload steps. The core is not a repeated recipe: each of the eight neutralizations is a DIFFERENT reasoned decision on a DIFFERENT corrective axis (cool frames warmed, warm frame cooled, greenish frame corrected on tint, underexposed frame lifted, overexposed frame recovered, near-neutral frame nudged small, genuinely-golden frame held) all forced to converge on one measurable target — the in-frame 18% grey card — before the agent's own warm-amber house look is propagated across the set, so a blanket batch correction or a per-frame auto_tone cannot pass. Layered on: a 5-way sponsor triage (vectorize the flat rasters vs select_by_prompt+remove_background the photographed marks — a wrong route is invisible until print), a genuine prep-before-trace vectorize of a skewed off-white kraft scan, and TWO one-file-per-row data-merges into two hand-authored single-record templates (schedule->artist pages, sponsors->recognition cards) with three image columns each. Respects every hard limit: no generative fill/expand, no text-to-image, no upscaling, no inpainting (the photographed marks are fully visible so the lift is a clean cutout), no from-scratch layout; convert_pdf_to_indd is NOT used (both templates are supplied authored .indd); image_crop_and_resize is downscale-only with onSubjectClipping='extract'; deprecated image_adjust_color_temperature / _vibrance_and_saturation are replaced by image_apply_adjustments; image_apply_auto_tone is NOT used (the look is authored from primitives). The multi-sponsor grid the original brief implied is correctly reshaped into one card per sponsor because the merge cannot place several records on a page.
hardness_rationale: FAILURE GATE (a wrong DECISION, not a self-measurement): (1) every performer photo carries a physical 18% grey card and the acceptance criterion is that each card, graded on its RETAINED pre-crop neutralized master (grey card still present), reads a clean neutral with the whole set matched to one white point under the agent's warm-amber house look — a target the agent can miss, and it must REPORT the final WB/exposure move per frame so 'matched' is verifiable rather than asserted; a naive agent that copies one white-balance across the batch, or runs per-frame auto_tone, leaves the cool frames blue, the warm frame orange and the greenish frame green and fails. (2) The 5-way sponsor triage: three flat rasters must be vectorized (stay razor-sharp), two photographed-on-a-busy-ground marks must be lifted (select_by_prompt+remove_background) — vectorizing a photo returns a blob of reflections/cloth, lifting a flat mark leaves it soft; the sources share a neutral same-kind .png scheme and the roster references a uniform basename, so the answer is nowhere in a supplied field and a wrong route is invisible until the mark is on the printer. (3) Card-exclusion is a SEPARATE gate on the delivered 4:5 crops (card cropped OUT), so neutrality is never graded on a card-removed file; and each merge adds a page-count = row-count gate (8 artist pages, 5 sponsor cards). HUMAN-HARD ELEMENTS: (a) cross-asset neutralization of eight differently-lit shots to a common measurable white point on differing axes (temperature vs green/magenta tint vs tonal), which a novice cannot match by eye; (b) the two-different-correct-treatments sponsor triage; (c) prep-before-trace discipline on a skewed, kraft-ground, margin-padded wordmark scan; (d) constraint-reasoning around tool limits — knockouts via remove_background not select->invert->fill, the impossible multi-sponsor grid reshaped to one card per sponsor, and the wordmark/kraft reaching the page only as merge binds (free-form placement banned). TRAP: the golden-hour act (frame 04) is genuinely warm and its card is already neutral, so the naive 'warm the cool cast' or 'cool an imagined cast' move strips its real color; the correct path reads THAT card and holds white balance. A second trap sits in the merge: a multi-sponsor grid or a convert_pdf_to_indd template both fail to bind, and only the supplied single-record authored templates merge. MEASURABLE ACCEPTANCE (decoupled so no artifact is graded on a region it crops away): grey card neutral (channel spread near zero) and one shared white point evaluated on all eight RETAINED masters; card-exclusion checked separately on the eight 4:5 crops; the agent reports per-frame WB/exposure params; every sponsor mark print-safe by the correct method; the wordmark a clean skew-free transparent-ground vector; and exactly one press-ready ~300 DPI page per roster row (8 + 5).
